solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Englishman in noted sloop heading out of port

parts.note: the Sloop John B is the boat in a famous folk song recorded by the Beach Boys

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word goes out of it

parts.note: Hull is an English port on the Humber estuary

explanation.surface: An Englishman sails aboard a famous sloop as it leaves harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading out of' removes the first letter H from HULL, leaving ULL.
explanation.definitionFit: The personification of England or the typical Englishman, a stout figure in a Union Jack waistcoat.

clue.text: Yank in Top Gear?

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to jerk
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American appears on the TV motoring show Top Gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb 'pull sharply'; 'Top Gear' is the BBC motoring show, read here as clothing worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting sleeveless jacket is a garment worn on the upper body, so playful 'top gear'.

clue.text: Gathering this early crop, for example

indicators.note: a gathering pulls things together into a new bunch, so the letters of the two words are collected and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing in this year's early crop is an example of harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' rearranges the letters of THIS and EARLY. 'Crop' looks agricultural, but it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is a very short cut of the hair, one example of a way of styling it.

clue.text: Order extremely elegant basin

parts.note: to bid is to command or order

indicators.note: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word elegant are taken

explanation.surface: A customer orders a very elegant washbasin.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin used for washing oneself, found in many bathrooms.

clue.text: Singles in catalogue, mostly female, with pride

indicators.note: the singles are placed inside the shortened catalogue
most of the word is kept, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
singles are ones, single units

explanation.surface: Single records listed in a catalogue are mostly by proud women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the catalogue word. 'Pride' looks like self-respect, but it is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat living with a pride, the collective noun for a group of lions.

clue.text: Simple book with a rather balmy section?

indicators.note: a section of the phrase rather balmy supplies the letters, straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A simple book contains a rather sunny, mild chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' is an old word for a medicinal plant, so a book about simples is a herbal.
explanation.definitionFit: A book describing plants and their medicinal uses; 'simples' are old-fashioned medicinal plants.

clue.text: Is Gainsbourg turned on or going out?

indicators.note: turned means the words Is and the singer's first name are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Serge Gainsbourg was a French singer-songwriter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether the French singer Gainsbourg is aroused or leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses IS SERGE (Gainsbourg's first name) to give EGRESSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of emerging or leaving, a formal synonym of exit.

clue.text: Unfinished sea food that's spicy

indicators.note: the word is left unfinished, its last letter removed

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe

explanation.surface: Half-eaten seafood that has a spicy kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the final C of BALTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy curry dish cooked and served in a metal bowl, popular in Birmingham, England.

clue.text: Glass apt to shatter at the eleventh hour

indicators.note: a glass that shatters breaks into pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Glass likely to break at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shatter' rearranges GLASS and APT. The answer is used as in 'at the last gasp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at the very last moment, just before it is too late.

clue.text: Bit of water in sink seen by artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist
taken as written
to sink is to drop

explanation.surface: A bit of water in the kitchen sink is noticed by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like the kitchen basin, but it is the verb meaning fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of falling rain is a tiny bit of water.

clue.text: Fine flowers with added features

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
flowers are things that flow, here small streams or rills

explanation.surface: Fine blooms bring extra decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' are not blooms but things that flow: rills are small streams.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills are unnecessary extras or embellishments, as in 'no-frills'.

clue.text: Touch instrument up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: Tune up a musical instrument by touching it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TUBA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things abut when they touch or border each other.

clue.text: Piece introduced for clique?

definitions.meaning: something added or set into a larger whole, such as a small map inside a larger one
read as two words, an ... is an exclusive group, the question mark flagging the pun

explanation.definitionFit: A small piece set into a larger one, while the 'in set' is a fashionable clique.

clue.text: English maiden giving orders for relief work

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
bossing means ordering people around

explanation.surface: An English girl bosses people around in charity aid work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief work' looks like aid, but it is raised decoration. A maiden is an over in cricket with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossing is raising a design in relief on a surface, such as metal or paper.

clue.text: Island where old king seizes power

indicators.note: seizes means the king's name grips the other letter inside it

parts.note: Cyrus the Great was an ancient Persian king
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An island where an ancient ruler takes control.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Sorry about writer? So much for the French!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pen is a writing implement
tant is French for so much

explanation.surface: An apology about a writer, dismissively waving away the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So much for the French!' looks like a dismissal, but it asks for the French for 'so much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone repentant feels remorse, so is sorry for what they did.

clue.text: TS Eliot represented ladies and gents

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet TS Eliot stood for ladies and gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges TS ELIOT. 'Ladies' and 'gents' are British names for public lavatories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ladies and the Gents are British signs for women's and men's public lavatories.

clue.text: High growth Swedes lie about

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swedes lie around in tall vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SWEDES and LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine flower growing high up in the mountains, so a plant of high places.

clue.text: Criminal dictates in crucial trial

indicators.note: criminal means bad or wrong, so the letters are shown in a corrupted order

explanation.surface: A criminal dictates terms in a key court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges DICTATES; 'trial' looks like a court case but is a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive test proving worth, from testing gold with acid.

clue.text: Indian pet to approach unnoticed

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American and First Nations people
a pup, a young dog, is a pet

explanation.surface: An Indian pet sneaks up on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep up is to move close to someone stealthily without being noticed.

clue.text: Father's not right in the head

indicators.note: not marks the following letter as one that is absent from the word

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old British schoolboy slang, for father; the possessive 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Father is not quite right in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's not right' reads as PATER without R.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the head, especially the top of it.

clue.text: Battle song that's timeless is about right

indicators.note: is about means the shortened song sits around the next letter
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: an anthem is a song

explanation.surface: A war song that endures forever concerns what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops the T from ANTHEM, making ANHEM, which 'is about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: A Second World War battle of 1944 fought at a bridge in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Articles about Dickens character losing it somewhere in Europe

indicators.note: the two articles go about, on either side of, the shortened character

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles

indicators.note: losing means the following word is dropped from the name

parts.note: Little Dorrit is the heroine of the Dickens novel of that name

explanation.surface: News articles about a Dickens heroine who has lost her charm somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' gives two of them, one on each side; 'losing it' looks like losing one's temper but drops the letters IT from the heroine of Little Dorrit.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Members of social elite dropping in to see composer

indicators.note: dropping means the next word is dropped from the longer one

parts.note: Brahmins are members of the highest Hindu caste, and by extension of a cultured elite

explanation.surface: Society people drop in to visit a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like visiting, but IN is dropped from BRAHMINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a nineteenth-century German composer.

clue.text: Set off with old-fashioned envelope for school

indicators.note: the word for old-fashioned acts as an envelope wrapped round the school

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Posting something with an outdated envelope to a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that has been set off has been exploded, or detonated.

clue.text: Heading for the championship

definitions.meaning: a heading at the top of a page or chapter
the champion's status, as in winning the world crown

explanation.definitionFit: A heading names a piece of writing, and a sports crown is held by the champion.

clue.text: Subordinate in Hereford, say

definitions.meaning: a Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, and cattle low, or moo, so one is something that lows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hereford' looks like the English city, but it is the breed of cattle, so a creature that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lower rank is junior; a cow that moos is jokingly 'one that lows'.

clue.text: Lowly dance in uncertain state

definitions.meaning: a Caribbean dance in which one bends back to pass under a low bar
a state of waiting, in suspense, with nothing decided

explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean dance goes very low under a bar; also a state of uncertainty.

clue.text: 10 runs

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 10 across, meaning added features or embellishments
in cricket, runs scored from byes, leg byes, wides and no-balls rather than off the bat

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs not scored off the bat (byes, wides, no-balls) are added to the total separately under their own heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional embellishments are optional add-ons; in cricket, bonus runs not hit by a batter.

clue.text: Dowdy swimmer keeps what's left

indicators.note: keeps means the swimmer holds the remainder inside itself

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
a rump is a remnant, what is left of something

explanation.surface: A shabby swimmer holds on to the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish describes someone unfashionable and dull in dress, like a frump.

clue.text: Doctor Jekyll's fourth compact

parts.note: to doctor is to treat medically

indicators.note: fourth means only the fourth letter of the name Jekyll is taken

explanation.surface: Dr Jekyll's fourth pact, perhaps with Mr Hyde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like Jekyll's title, but it is the verb meaning treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a formal agreement between parties, a synonym of a pact or accord.

clue.text: Charlie stirs drinks boisterously

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to stir is to arouse or rouse

explanation.surface: Charlie stirs up drinks noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink plenty of alcohol and make merry in a noisy, lively way.
